# Ferrule

> A local key vault for LLM provider keys, with an OpenAI-compatible router in front of
> it. One Go binary. Keys are encrypted on the user's own disk; nothing is hosted.

Ferrule is a **key vault first, a router second**. A person pastes a provider key once;
Ferrule becomes the single encrypted local home for it. The unified endpoint, the model
board, the alias ladders, and the spend/egress views all fall out of that.

If you are an agent driving Ferrule, read this file and then call `brief`. Do not explore.

## Two things it does that alternatives do not

- **Zero-config discovery.** No config file. It scans localhost for running runtimes
  (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp) and adopts them; a cloud provider is *paste a key*.
- **Egress visibility.** A local, metadata-only ledger of what actually left the machine,
  per app and per model — classified from the address the connection was made to.

## The three faces (they do not overlap)

| Face | Path | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| Inference — raw tokens | `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/images/generations`, `/v1/models` | Ferrule app token, Bearer |
| Inference — media passthrough | `/p/<source>/…`, provider's native shape, bytes unaltered | Ferrule app token |
| Control | `/api/op/<name>`, `/mcp` | localhost + a per-run control token |

The control face is **not** an inference path. Your own inference goes through the
OpenAI-compatible endpoint like any other client.

## Driving inference

```
OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8899/v1
OPENAI_API_KEY=frl_…        # a Ferrule app token, never a provider key
```

The `model` field resolves in this order, first hit wins:

1. an **alias** (`fast`, `smart`, `cheap`, `local`) → its ordered ladder, dark rungs skipped
2. a **remap** → an alias, or `source/model`
3. `source/model` → that exact pair (source id or display name)
4. a bare **model id** → the first live source serving it, local preferred

An alias that exists but has no reachable rung is an **error**, never a fall-through to a
same-named model elsewhere. A rung that fails with a transport error, 5xx, or 429 falls
to the next; a 4xx does not.

## Driving the control plane (MCP)

`GET /mcp` returns the tool manifest. `POST /mcp` speaks JSON-RPC: `initialize`,
`tools/list`, `tools/call`. The manifest is generated from the same command bus the panel
and the CLI dispatch through, so it is always a superset of what the UI can do.

**Read ops** answer immediately: `brief`, `status`, `list_sources`, `list_models`,
`list_aliases`, `get_alias`, `list_remaps`, `usage_summary`, `egress_summary`,
`list_grants`, `list_staged`.

**Mutating ops stage; they never land on their own.** `add_source`, `refresh_source`,
`remove_source`, `detect_local`, `set_alias`, `remove_alias`, `set_remap`,
`remove_remap`, `revoke_grant`, `set_setting`, `catalog_refresh`. A staged op returns an
id; a person applies it. Do not wait on one landing.

**Person-only ops are refused at your door and are marked so in the manifest**, not
hidden from it: `mint_grant`, `export_config`, `import_config`, `read_content`,
`forget_content`. A provider key is stripped from any staged payload — including from
undeclared fields and from a URL's query string — and supplied by the person at apply
time.

### `brief` — call this first

One bounded read of the whole situation: every source with `status`, `code`, `reason`,
`remedy`; a *summary* of servable models by capability and location; aliases with the
rung actually serving each; grant counts; staged ops; 24h egress; the last five failures;
the last five control calls; the closed reason vocabulary; and the short list of moves
that would change any of it. It grows with configured sources and aliases — never with
the model catalog, the ledger, or the control log.

Useful shape: `list_models {where: "local"|"cloud", capability: "chat"|"vision"|…,
max_cost: <USD per Mtok>}` answers "cheapest model with vision" directly.

## The reason vocabulary (closed — branch on the code, never parse the message)

```
ok · unreachable · bad_key · bad_status · no_models · local_no_models
test_failed · test_timeout · unknown_provider · needs_key · needs_base_url
insecure_url · redirect
```

Every non-`ok` code carries a `remedy` naming the exact next move. The live list is
published in `brief.reason_codes`.

## CLI

`ferrule status [--json]` · `serve` · `add [provider] [--test-model ID]` ·
`open` · `startup [on|off]` · `ls sources|models|aliases` · `refresh <source>` ·
`rm <source>` · `alias` · `remap` · `key` · `usage [--egress|--content N]` · `export` · `import` ·
`version`

`ferrule serve` on a port another Ferrule already holds exits **0** — a login item and a
double-clicked app both ask for the same thing and it is already true. A port held by
anything else is still an error.

Exit codes map one-to-one to next actions: **0** worked · **1** did not, and the reason
says why · **2** the invocation was wrong.

Keys are never accepted as flags — they are read from the terminal without echo, or from
stdin when piped.

## Constraints worth knowing before you act

- **The control plane is loopback-only, always.** It needs a per-run token the daemon
  hands only to the page it serves; a cross-origin caller cannot obtain it.
- **The inference endpoints are shared with the local network by default**, and only
  those. Sharing is the `sharing` setting (`on`|`off`, default on), checked on the peer
  address of each accepted connection, so the panel's switch takes effect on the next
  request with no restart. `--host 127.0.0.1` closes the port outright; no setting
  reopens it.
  The control routes refuse any connection whose peer is not loopback, so `/api`, `/mcp`
  and the panel answer 403 from another machine no matter what token is presented. If you
  are running on a machine other than the daemon's, you have the inference face and not
  the control face — do not report a 403 there as a bug.
- **A key never travels over http** to anything but loopback unless explicitly
  acknowledged, and no client follows a redirect while carrying one.
- **Ferrule does not run models.** llama.cpp, Ollama, and the providers do inference.
- **Media is not normalized.** Prediction-based providers ride the passthrough lane in
  their own shape; do not expect Replicate at `/v1`.
- **Content logging is off by default**, stored apart from the metadata ledger, and
  person-only to read.
- The one request Ferrule makes on its own behalf is a background fetch of the public
  model-capability catalog. It carries nothing about the user and can be turned off.

## Source

- `SPEC.md` — the built system's contract; §0 is the agent contract, and each clause
  names the test that fails if it stops holding.
- `FERRULE.md` — vision, roadmap, and the original handoff.
- `README.md` — the human face.
- `make demo` — a whole Ferrule with fake providers, no keys needed.
